title: Excessive abstention is deliberately left without a numerical threshold and judged as a pattern
content:
A.1.6.2.1.1 opens by separating two things a participation metric would conflate: "abstaining refers to casting an Abstain vote, not to failing to vote entirely (which is addressed under A.1.6.2.1)." An abstention satisfies the 75% participation requirement while contributing nothing to a decision — so without a separate rule, abstaining on everything would be perfect compliance.

The Atlas accepts legitimate abstention — "appropriate when an Aligned Delegate has a conflict of interest or lacks sufficient expertise on a specialized matter" — but insists it "should be the exception rather than the norm," grounded in the role's purpose: "The Aligned Delegate role exists to provide active stewardship of Sky Governance."

Enforcement is then deliberately unquantified. The Core Facilitator weighs (1) the proportion of abstentions over six months, (2) "whether the Aligned Delegate provided reasoning for abstentions," and (3) "whether the pattern suggests avoidance of accountability rather than conflict of interest or insufficient expertise." The document states outright that it "does not establish a specific numerical threshold... Rather, the Core Facilitator exercises reasonable judgment in identifying patterns."

The refusal to set a number is the decision worth noting, and it contrasts sharply with the neighbouring rules — 75%, six months, three business days, one week, 90 days, 1-2 days. Those are all specified. The difference is what each rule targets: participation is a countable act, while abstention is only problematic *because of what it indicates*, and the third factor makes that explicit by asking about avoidance of accountability. A numerical cap on a motive-dependent behaviour would be trivially gameable — abstain just under the line — and would also punish a delegate with genuinely many conflicts.

The cost is a discretionary standard in a framework that elsewhere distrusts discretion. The mitigation is the reasoning factor: a delegate who explains each abstention builds their own defence, which converts the discretion into something evidence can answer.
description: A.1.6.2.1.1 distinguishes abstaining from not voting, names three factors including whether the pattern suggests avoidance of accountability, and explicitly declines to set a number.
